reddit_body:
We are telling the story of SpaceCorps 2027 one release at a time, and it starts in a browser tab. Back on January 11, 2026, we shipped update 0.0.5 of our browser prototype, the game SpaceCorps 2027 was later rebuilt from.

That release was the foundation. We wrote the real-time game loop and synced player positions over SignalR, so several pilots could share a map. Combat worked ship to ship and ship to alien, with damage, shields and ammo use, and aliens fought back when you shot them. You could jump through portals between maps, read your coordinates on a minimap, take quests, buy from a shop with item rarities, and fit your ship in a drag-and-drop hangar. There was a ranking, player statistics and an in-game wiki too.

Eight months later we rebuilt the whole thing as a native game, and the next posts in this series walk through how we got there.

If you played the browser version back then, what do you remember most from it?

Next stop in our look back: update 0.0.6 of the browser prototype, released on January 11, 2026, the same day as the foundation release.

The headline was Skylab, a base-building feature that sat next to the flying. You managed its modules, produced resources with them and toggled each module's power on or off. We liked the idea of something that keeps working for you between fights, and it gave the resources a place to come from.

The same release added Assembly, the system for crafting items, so those resources had somewhere to go. It also brought more alien types and loot drops, and a static delay before shields start to recharge. That last one changed combat more than it sounds: after a hit you had to back off for a moment instead of tanking forever. On the hangar side, we removed drag-and-select because people kept selecting items by accident.

This was still the browser version. SpaceCorps 2027, the native rebuild, came eight months later.

We are looking back at every release of SpaceCorps 2027, and this one comes with footage from the time. On January 17, 2026, we shipped update 0.0.10 of our browser prototype.

Boosters got most of the work. The clip shows the booster panel as it was: Damage, Shield, Hitpoints, Experience, Honor, Resources and Luck, each with its own timer counting down. The rest of the update was about safety and repair. Safe zones changed size: portals became 1.5x smaller and bases 2x larger. Repairs now stopped the moment you took damage, waited out a cooldown, and had to be restarted by hand. The settings menu started to highlight a key bound to two actions, and the hotbar stopped forgetting its items between sessions. There were new map sectors to explore as well.

SpaceCorps 2027 was rebuilt as a native game eight months later, so this panel is a piece of history.

We rebuilt the SpaceCorps space MMO as a native desktop game for Windows, macOS and Linux. The core stayed familiar. Before this, every version meant a trip to the download page. From 0.2.1 on, new versions downloaded in the background and installed when you clicked Restart to Update, or when you quit. Settings got an About page with Check for Updates and two switches, both on by default. The game only installed updates signed by SpaceCorps with matching checksums, tested a new version before keeping it, and put the old one back if the new one does not start. Nothing interrupts you in the middle of a flight.

That one change is why the rest of this series moves so fast: shipping a fix stopped costing players a manual download.

The same release fixed the repair drone, which had done nothing after a launch until your loadout changed. Its slot glows while it repairs, and you get a message when repairs start, stop or get interrupted.

reddit_title: 0.2.3, September: absorbance started deciding how much of each hit your shields take in our space MMO
reddit_body:
On September 26, 2026, update 0.2.3 of SpaceCorps 2027 fixed something that had been quietly wrong since launch: what your shields actually do.

Until then every hit went 80% to your shields and 20% to your hull, whatever you had fitted. From 0.2.3, your absorbance became your shields' share of each hit. A Light Shield Core alone is 70%, a Basic 80%, a Heavy 85%, and shield cells add 2%, 4% or 6% each, up to 100%. A Basic Shield Core with two Advanced cells comes to 88%, so your hull takes 12% instead of 20%. When shields run out, the hull takes the whole hit, as before.

Modules got the same treatment. Adaptive Cores finally gave their bonuses, after adding nothing and even halving absorbance. Shields slowed your ship again, as the item cards always said. The hangar started showing the split under your combat stats, so you can see it before you launch.

Aliens kept the old 80/20 split.

How do you fit your ship now: more shield cells for absorbance, or thrusters for speed?

reddit_title: 0.3.0, September: our free space MMO split into three worlds
reddit_body:
Back in September, on the 26th, update 0.3.0 split the SpaceCorps 2027 galaxy into three separate worlds: Alpha, Beta and Gamma.

Until then pilots of every tier flew the same sectors and met the same aliens. From 0.3.0, each world had its own copy of every sector, its own aliens and its own pilots, and you only met the ones in your world. Your account stayed shared: items, credits, clan, the season and the leaderboards.

The worlds differed in risk and pay. Alien strength went 1.0x, 1.5x and 2.0x, while kill and quest pay went 1.0x, 2.0x and 3.0x, so a higher world clearly earned more per hour. PvP opened up as you climbed: only some sectors in Alpha, everywhere in Gamma. Safe zones and the Peace Protocol protected you in all three.

You picked a world at Setup, once per season, and each took up to 1,000 pilots. Moving was possible only at the Blackhole Eruption on day 30.

There are five of them, Laser Optics I to V, each a Skylab research and a craftable Extra. Fit one in an Extras slot and it adds +2, +4, +6, +8 or +10 points to your laser hit chance, held at 100 %. They do not stack: only the best one you have fitted counts. A pilot at 80 % with Optics III reads 86.0 % in the Hangar.

The price is the Extras slot itself and the crafting: Optics V takes 24 hours of research and 75,000 Thulium among other parts.

When we shipped it, nobody had flown the new numbers yet; they came from the game files and tests.

Is an Extras slot worth spending on hit chance, or do you keep it for something else?

reddit_body:
Back in November, update 0.5.7 added the Miyuki, a ship made for keeping other pilots alive. You research it in the Skylab after the Paragon, build level I in the Assembly, and then turn that same ship into level II, III, IV and V. Its fit and everything installed stay on it, and a level cannot be skipped or bought.

Its tools are links. Channel Heal, from level II, ties you to a friendly ship of your group or company within 1,200 units, and for 5 s that ship gets 50,000 hull a second. Channel Shield links to a friend's shield the same way. Its Heal Pod also lasts 7.5 s instead of 5 s.

An honest note from the time: nobody had flown most of the update's numbers yet when it shipped, and we said so in the notes.

The same update rebuilt the Forge around sockets and added 44 missions for levels 11 to 14.

Would you fly support in a group, or do you always want the damage seat?

reddit_body:
Back in November, update 0.5.8 gave the aliens tiers. A Greek letter in front of an alien's name shows its tier, and the tier sets both how tough it is and what it pays.

Alpha is the base. Beta is 1.5 times as tough and pays 2 times. Gamma is 2 times as tough and pays 3 times. And Delta, which was added in this update, is 4 times as tough and pays 6 times. Each world rolls the tiers of its aliens from a table, so the same map can hold an easy target next to a hard one.

The same update also made your own rocket blast hurt you for half of what it does to others, added controller support, and Premium stopped doubling experience. We said at the time that nobody had flown most of the new numbers yet.

Do you go looking for Delta aliens, or steer round them?

reddit_body:
This is the last post in our look back. Update 0.5.10 shipped on November 20, and with it the story has caught up with the game as it is now.

The headline was Davidski's Nightmare getting much harder. Every ship of the gate deals 3 times the damage. Evil Davidski has 10 times the hull and shield, 5,500,000 hull and 6,600,000 shield. And he cannot be hurt at all while any golden ship lives. In 0.5.9 a fifth of the damage got through; that is gone, so you have to destroy the golden ships first. His rocket barrages now fire Dormant Lances, the homing rockets that follow you.

The same update gave the clan dungeons a third Phantom's Lance illusion, added an emote wheel (hold N), personal loot crates for groups, and a 25 % chance for a Forge tier-up to put a free buff into an empty socket.

Thanks for reading along from the browser prototype to here.

Which part of the whole story would you like us to go back and improve?
